cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: An instantaneous unstable alignment does not determine system stability; the decisive object is whether the closed-loop dynamics reinforce or cancel that alignment while respecting the global resource budget.
common_abstraction: instantaneous positive feedback can be large without causing finite-time failure
trajectory-level feedback law matters more than a static snapshot
global resource/localization constraints can exclude otherwise admissible local states

global resource budget -> finite energy and spatial decay
shared_constraints: must distinguish locally admissible but globally invalid states
disanalogies: Navier-Stokes is infinite-dimensional, nonlinear and nonlocal

cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Require every geometry-based candidate to discriminate both finite-energy non-solution fields and exact non-decaying solution fields; only a quantity using the intersection of exact dynamics and global finite-energy localization survives.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Construct one finite-energy smooth divergence-free field with strong local positive-eigenframe alignment and one exact Navier-Stokes linear flow with the same alignment but infinite energy; a viable route must explain why both are excluded for different explicit reasons.
